title: Crypto Market Turning Point End of Altcoins? Bitcoin Price Analysis
subTitle:
The market is starting to feel different. Not dead. Not euphoric. Just… different.
Recently we saw news that BlackRock bought around $175 million worth of Bitcoin through its ETF, the iShares Bitcoin Trust. Last year, this kind of headline was normal. Almost every week institutions were adding thousands of BTC, ETF inflows were strong, and holdings were expanding. That steady demand created confidence and pushed price structure higher.
Now in 2026, the tone feels mixed. Some days we see inflows. Other days we see outflows and headlines about reduced holdings. But this is not about emotion. It is about capital flow. When investors put money into the ETF, Bitcoin gets bought. When they redeem shares, Bitcoin gets sold. The ETF is reacting to demand. It is not predicting the market.
Now let’s talk price. This is where things get serious.
If Bitcoin is holding above $70,000 on strong higher-timeframe structure, the market remains constructive. Above that level, dips are likely to be treated as pullbacks, not breakdowns. Liquidity stays inside the system. Altcoins may struggle against BTC dominance, but the broader crypto structure remains intact. Confidence survives.
But if Bitcoin drops below $70,000 with strong volume and fails to reclaim it quickly, that is where risk increases. Below that level, the psychology shifts. What looked like consolidation starts looking like distribution. ETF outflows can accelerate. Retail sentiment weakens. And altcoins usually suffer more because they depend on Bitcoin stability to perform.
Historically, Bitcoin leads every major phase. When institutions enter, they choose Bitcoin first because it is the deepest liquidity pool in crypto. Altcoins outperform later in the cycle when liquidity is abundant and risk appetite is high. When uncertainty rises, capital rotates back to Bitcoin. And when fear expands, capital exits the space entirely.
That is why calling this the “end of altcoins” is dramatic. It is not about death. It is about rotation and dominance. If Bitcoin stays strong above key structure, altcoins can recover in waves. If Bitcoin weakens below major levels, altcoins will bleed harder and faster.
Right now we are in a transition phase. ETF flows, macro pressure, profit taking, and positioning are all colliding. Easy money conditions are fading. Liquidity is more selective. Strong projects will survive. Weak narratives will disappear.
So what matters most?
Watch Bitcoin price around $70,000. Watch ETF flows. Watch dominance. The market always shows strength or weakness at key levels before the big move happens.
This is not necessarily the end of anything. It may simply be the moment where the market decides who leads the next phase.

title: Ethereum Is Getting Better… So Why Is ETH Still Weak?
subTitle:
The newly released Protocol Priorities 2026 roadmap arrives at a time when markets are less interested in long-term vision statements and more focused on measurable outcomes, economic impact, and risk structure improvements.
The roadmap outlines Ethereum’s next development phase across three strategic pillars:
• Scaling throughput and data availability
• Improving user experience (UX)
• Strengthening Layer-1 resilience and security
While highly technical in nature, the market’s central question is straightforward: Will these priorities help ETH recover during bearish conditions, and do they improve Ethereum’s economic structure rather than merely boosting developer sentiment?
Instead of promoting a single headline upgrade, the foundation presents a system-level thesis: Ethereum can increase throughput, reduce usability friction, and strengthen base-layer security simultaneously. If proven, this could lower ETH’s perceived risk premium and support higher long-term valuation as the dominant settlement layer for on-chain assets.
Scaling: Where the Economic Thesis Gets Tested
The most market-relevant component of the 2026 roadmap is scaling.
The Ethereum community recently increased the gas limit from 30 million to 60 million, the first major increase since 2021, with ambitions to move toward — and eventually exceed — 100 million gas, alongside improved execution efficiency and data availability structures.
This is more than a technical tweak. It reflects direct competitive pressure across the current cycle: Ethereum must support greater economic activity without pricing out users, while preserving decentralization and neutrality — qualities valued by traditional financial institutions.
Two scaling components stand out:
• ePBS (enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation)
This design aims to reduce block-building centralization risks and limit distortions caused by MEV (Maximal Extractable Value). A more neutral and predictable block production process could reduce a long-term structural risk embedded in Ethereum.
• zkEVM Attester Client
Transitioning from experimental to operational readiness, this component signals that future scaling will not rely solely on external rollups. Instead, proof verification and attestation mechanisms may integrate deeper into Ethereum’s core stack — a structure that institutions can more easily evaluate and trust.
Together, these efforts aim not just to increase throughput but to maintain Ethereum’s economic relevance while minimizing perceived tradeoffs.
UX Improvements & L1 Hardening Could Reduce Long-Term Risk Discounts
The roadmap’s other two pillars — usability improvements and base-layer hardening — may attract less media attention but could significantly impact long-term valuation.
Native Account Abstraction & Smart Wallet Defaults
In 2026, usability efforts focus on making smart-contract wallets the default experience through native account abstraction and interoperability improvements.
Proposals such as EIP-7701 and EIP-8141 aim to embed smart account logic directly into the protocol, reducing reliance on complex bundlers and relayers.
This is not merely a product design improvement — it is a market adoption issue.
Wallet friction remains one of the largest barriers to mainstream adoption. Lower fees alone cannot drive mass adoption if onboarding remains complex and error-prone. Reducing signature steps, simplifying cross-chain interactions, and improving default safety settings could significantly improve retention among users and enterprises.
These improvements also align with post-quantum readiness planning, offering a cleaner transition path beyond current ECDSA signature schemes — a forward-looking factor often valued by long-term capital allocators.
Strengthening Layer-1 Security and Neutrality
Base-layer resilience remains central to Ethereum’s institutional credibility.
Security and neutrality initiatives include:
• Trillion Dollar Security Initiative
• Trustless RPC infrastructure
• FOCIL research (censorship resistance)
• Statelessness research
• Expanded testing infrastructure and upgrade cadence
These initiatives aim to ensure Ethereum remains secure, neutral, and predictable under stress — critical requirements if the network is to support stablecoins, tokenized assets, and large-scale financial settlement.
Fee Metrics Are Weakening the Valuation Narrative
Despite ambitious long-term plans, ETH valuation remains heavily influenced by current on-chain data.
Gas prices are extremely low, around 0.038 gwei, and daily transaction fees are estimated near 140 ETH, down roughly 40% year-over-year.
This is beneficial for users and developers, enabling broader adoption. However, it weakens the post-EIP-1559 value narrative: if fees remain low, burn rates remain weak, reducing supply-compression effects.
Ethereum may be winning on utility while appearing “weak” on the metric many investors monitor first.
Meanwhile, economic activity continues migrating to Layer-2 networks. Vitalik Buterin has acknowledged that the original L2 vision is evolving and that Ethereum may need a path less dependent on L2 value capture.
The key unresolved question: how much value generated on L2 ultimately flows back to ETH — and how long that transmission takes.
When Could the Roadmap Support ETH Price Recovery?
The roadmap may support ETH during bearish conditions, but primarily by improving long-term fundamentals rather than triggering immediate upside.
This view aligns with perspectives from 21Shares, which suggest ETH’s upside potential depends on whether Layer-2 growth:
• stimulates burn mechanisms, or
• strengthens structural value capture tied to mainnet economics.
If Ethereum surpasses 100M gas, expands blob capacity efficiently, delivers native smart-wallet UX, and maintains censorship resistance and base-layer security, it increases the probability of retaining its role as the preferred settlement layer for tokenized assets and on-chain finance.
However, a technical roadmap alone cannot reverse ETF flows or immediately restore high fee revenue. It improves the structural setup for growth — but price response still requires capital inflows and sustained economic activity.

title: ETH CIRCULATION UP 950K SINCE MERGE
subTitle:
New data from Odaily shows Ethereum's supply has grown by over 950,000 units since the Merge upgrade completed.
Total circulation now sits at approximately 121.5 million ETH.
Annual inflation rate is around 0.23%.
For context: Before the Merge, Ethereum was inflationary at around 3-4% annually. The shift to proof-of-stake was supposed to make ETH "ultrasound money" with net supply reduction during high network activity.
But here we are. Supply is slowly ticking up.

Why? Lower network fees mean less ETH burned. When demand drops, issuance outpaces burns.
This doesn't break the Ethereum thesis. But it kills the "ultrasound money" narrative for now.

Still, 0.23% inflation is lower than Bitcoin's upcoming sub-1% rate post-halving. And far lower than the 2-3% fiat inflation central banks target.
The question: Does supply growth matter when adoption keeps expanding?

title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump's Global Tariffs, Boosting Crypto Relief Rally
subTitle:
The U.S. Supreme Court delivered a major setback to President Donald Trump's economic agenda on February 20, 2026, ruling 6-3 that his sweeping global tariffs, imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), exceeded presidential authority and were unlawful!
Chief Justice John Roberts wrote the majority opinion, stating that the 1977 law did not grant the president power to unilaterally impose broad import levies on nearly every trading partner. The decision invalidated most of the tariffs enacted last year, potentially opening the door to billions in refunds for importers who paid the duties (estimates from prior collections exceed $130-200 billion, though the Court did not address repayment details). 
In a defiant response, Trump denounced the justices as "fools" and "disgraceful," then swiftly imposed a new 10% across the board global tariff under alternative trade laws, set to take effect soon. This ruling reduces immediate trade war escalation and policy uncertainty that had weighed on global markets...
Impact on Cryptocurrency The decision provided short term relief to risk assets, including crypto. Bitcoin briefly surged about 2% post-ruling (climbing above $68,000 before pulling back), and the broader market saw a "relief bounce" as eased trade tensions boosted investor sentiment and liquidity expectations.
Key factors influencing crypto:
Reduced inflation and trade uncertainty, Tariffs had fueled inflation fears and economic slowdown risks, pressuring risk-on assets like cryptocurrencies. Striking down the broad tariffs eases these pressures, supporting higher liquidity flows into volatile markets such as Bitcoin and altcoins.Market volatility dynamics, Previous tariff threats (e.g., escalations with China) triggered massive liquidations and sell-offs in crypto, wiping out billions due to leveraged positions. The Court's invalidation removes a major uncertainty driver, potentially stabilizing sentiment and encouraging inflows.Political and policy implications, While modest in direct impact so far, the ruling shifts focus in Washington, possibly freeing bandwidth for crypto-friendly policies (e.g., regulatory clarity or innovation support). However, Trump's pivot to new tariffs introduces ongoing uncertainty, tempering gains.
Overall, the ruling favors a positive near-term outlook for crypto by curbing aggressive protectionism, though traders remain watchful of the administration's next moves and potential retaliatory actions from trading partners...
